example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, September, against the FY26 Board Budget. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

messages.text: Can you compare September with our budget? Profit came in lower than we planned.
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which entity, or which set of entities?
Which period: the month, the quarter to date or the year to date? Is that period closed?
Which budget, by name: the original, a revised budget or the latest forecast?
What are your thresholds, as an amount and a percentage? Must a gap pass both, or either one?
Which one-time items fell in the period?
What driver data do you have? I need units, prices and headcount, with the budget's own figures for them.
Which grouping of lines does your management read?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading only. September, the month, and it is closed. Compare to the FY26 Board Budget. $5,000 and 10%, either one. No one-offs that I know of. The budget assumed 2,800 units at $150. Use the chart as it is.

messages.label: Checked the workspace, the company file and the budgets
rows: Enabled, so both sides come from the books
More than one version, includes FY26 Board Budget
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I compare **Northbrook Trading**'s actuals for **September** with the **FY26 Board Budget**, both read from your books. September is closed, so the report is final. A line needs commentary when it passes **$5,000 or 10%**. The prior year shows as a separate column. Shall I start?

messages.label: Read both sides in one batch
rows: Includes $8,000 paid to a law firm
messages.summary: 12 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Both sides use the accrual basis. One account is on one side only. **Insurance** shows $7,200 in September, and the budget has $0 for it. I show the $7,200 with the flag **no budget**, and I do not divide by zero.
Net income is **$23,900** below the budget. Each line adds its effect on profit:

card.title: Budget to actual net income, September
rows: Budget net income, FY26 Board Budget

messages.after: Six of seven lines pass $5,000 or 10%, so they get commentary. Payroll is $3,000 and 3.1% over. It is below both thresholds, so I note it and do not explain it.

messages.text: Revenue is $32,000 favourable, but that hides a lower price. I split revenue and cost of goods sold into volume and price. The parts add to each line, with $0 unexplained.

card.title: Drivers
head: Line and driver
Amount
How
F/U
rows: Cost of goods sold, unit cost

messages.after: Most of the cost overrun comes from the extra units that also raised revenue. The invoices show lower prices. They do not show the reason, so the price cause stays **to be confirmed**.

messages.text: Part of the shortfall is timing. It moved between months and will reverse:

card.title: Timing in the shortfall
rows: − Trade-show deposit for November, in marketing

messages.after: When October closes, its actuals can prove the insurance timing. The other $6,000 in marketing is higher ad cost, and it is permanent. Over the 3 remaining months, the arithmetic gives **$18,000**. Whether it continues is your call.

messages.text: Two causes are not in your books. G&A is $9,500 over. The ledger shows **$8,000 paid to a law firm** and $1,500 of smaller items. It shows the payee, not the reason. Other income is $600 below the budget, and the ledger does not show why. I do not guess a cause. Who owns these open items and the price question?
The financial controller owns G&A, other income and insurance. The sales director owns the price question. The marketing lead owns marketing.
Here is the commentary for your management meeting. Each line says where its cause comes from:

card.title: Commentary
head: Line
Variance
Cause
Owner
rows: Volume +$60,000. Price −$28,000, cause to be confirmed
$12,000 trade-show deposit, timing. $6,000 ad cost, permanent
$8,000 to a law firm, cause to be confirmed

messages.after: Your report has six sheets: the summary, the commentary, the drivers, the full-year outlook, the waterfall data and the coverage. The header names the FY26 Board Budget and the either rule. Do you want the report as an Excel file?

messages.text: Here is **BvA_Analysis_2026-09_NorthbrookTrading.xlsx**. I revise no budget and post nothing. A person decides what to change. Do you want me to save your settings for next month?
Done. For Northbrook Trading, I saved the thresholds, the either rule, the budget version, the line structure and the owners. I never save the figures, the commentary or the outlook.
